# Troubleshooting

The `qdjj-solver solve` command returns exit status **0** after saving a result and **2** for
recognized errors in input, required libraries, numerical calculations or file access; invalid
command arguments also return 2. With DMRG's default `require_convergence=False`, exit 0 can
accompany `Finite-problem checks passed: False`; set `require_convergence=true` in JSON when a
calculation must meet those checks. For continuum calculations, also assess bath
convergence through refinement ([numerics](numerics.md)).

To report a problem, provide a small input file that reproduces it, the error message,
the software version and any version information saved with the result on the
[issue page](https://github.com/rokzitko/qdjj_solver/issues).

Messages are abridged; the source is `docs/troubleshooting.toml`, and every quoted message is
checked against the error messages in the code.

## Input files, models and static calculations

| Message or symptom | What to check |
|---|---|
| DMRG/TeNPy or HDF5 dependency missing | From the source directory, run `python -m pip install '.[dmrg]'` with the interpreter used for the calculation. |
| The configuration or one of its sections (`model`, `bath`, `sector`, `solver`) must be an object | Use `{...}` for these objects, JSON booleans for yes/no settings and integers for sector values. Check the reported field path for typos. |
| Hamiltonian does not conserve `S_z` | For spin-mixing terms or spin-flip drives choose `Sector(parity, twice_sz=None)`, or JSON `"twice_sz": null`. |
| Fermion parity and `twice_sz` are incompatible | Even parity requires an even integer `twice_sz`; odd parity an odd one. |
| Empty symmetry sector, or more eigenpairs requested than states | Check the quantum numbers, the QP cutoff, the included modes and the number of requested eigenstates. |
| Invalid QP cutoff | Use `0 <= cutoff <= h.bath_modes` after model compression, or `None` (JSON `null`) for the full space. Set `cutoff` explicitly to 0 or `null` for impurity-only QP command-line inputs. |
| Sector dimension exceeds `max_dimension` | Estimate the basis size (`qpsolver dimension`) before raising `max_dimension`; consider a converged QP cutoff or DMRG. |
| An array needs more memory than `max_memory_gib` | The message names the array and a method or option that avoids it. Raise `max_memory_gib` only if the machine has that much free memory. |
| Sparse matrix exceeds `max_nnz` | Dense, sparse and Schur methods build this matrix. Check both `max_nnz` and the memory-derived cap from `max_memory_gib`, or use `method="matrix-free"`, whose basis and Krylov-space limits still apply. |
| The iterative eigensolver missed eigenvalues below the diagonal bound | ARPACK missed some of the lowest eigenvalues, even after a second spectral shift. Use `method="dense"` if the dimension allows it, or change `seed` or `ncv`, and report the case. |
| DMRG requires `cutoff=null` | Omit the JSON cutoff or set it to `null`; the MPS bond dimension `chi_max` controls the approximation. |
| Finite-problem convergence failed | Inspect residuals, orthonormality, energy ordering and sweep histories; increase the bond dimension, the number of sweeps or the number of initial-state trials as appropriate. |
| Initial or compared states have incompatible coordinates or layout | Reusing MPS states requires the same canonical basis, mode ordering and site grouping; start a new calculation if these change. |
| No supported state artifact, or checkpoint missing | Save with `save_states=True` or `--save-states`, and keep both the JSON and its named wavefunction file. |
| Checksum or scalar-record mismatch | Recover the matching JSON and wavefunction files from the same save. Editing the JSON invalidates the checksum that links it to the wavefunction file. |

## Floquet calculations, matrix elements and spectra

| Message or symptom | What to check |
|---|---|
| The canonical coordinates change during the drive period | Keep the gap and bath grid fixed. Build the model with `symmetry=False, compress=False`, and with `bath_reference="isolated"` when phases or direct hopping are driven. |
| Fourier interpolation error ... increase samples | Increase `samples` to resolve the relevant drive harmonics. |
| Too few Floquet candidates for the tracked states | The Floquet cutoff is too small for the spread of the sidebands; increase `floquet_cutoff` (or `eigenpairs_per_target` for shift-invert). |
| Two tracked states are replicas of one Floquet state | A small Floquet cutoff cuts a resonant chain of replicas; increase `floquet_cutoff` (use $M\gtrsim5$ even for weak drives). |
| Floquet weight below `tracking_threshold` | A tracked state is strongly hybridized; increase `floquet_cutoff`, `eigenpairs_per_target` or `basis_states`, lower `tracking_threshold`, or use `selection="all"`. |
| `basis_states` splits a degenerate static multiplet | Choose the static basis size $K$ at a gap of the static spectrum. |
| Sambe dimension exceeds `max_dimension` | Use `basis="eigen"`, a smaller static basis or fewer harmonics. |
| `selection='all'` with shift-invert | Use `method="dense"` (with `basis="eigen"` for large models) or give explicit `targets`. |
| Floquet states of different drives or scalar gauges | Build both results from one `PeriodicHamiltonian` with the same `drop_scalar_harmonics`. |
| No harmonic of the probe connects the sectors | Choose a destination sector compatible with the change in parity and spin induced by the probe. |
| Probe observable was not sampled, or the model lacks it | Build the `PeriodicHamiltonian` with `observables=True`, from a model that declares the observable. |
| The computed states split a degenerate static multiplet | Increase `states` or `basis_states`, or pass `merge_degenerate=False` to `lines`. |
| Physical operators require an uncompressed electron map | Electron probes (`d_up`, `spin_x`, ...) and `physical_operator` need a model built with `compress=False`. A model assembled directly as a `Hamiltonian` declares no electron map: pass an operator built with `create` and `annihilate` instead of a probe name. |
| The probe images need more memory than `max_memory_gib` | Restrict `ket_states` or raise `max_memory_gib`. |
